title: Cancer: the shocks stop
on December 5
summary: Rahu and Ketu, the north and south nodes, change signs on December 5. What ends for a Cancer Moon that day, what begins in love and in yourself, and how to use the next year and a half.

inside: What Rahu and Ketu, the north and south nodes, are
What ends for you on December 5 and what begins
How to use the eighteen months that follow, step by step
intro: If you are a Cancer by Moon sign, the last year and a half may have felt like a run of surprises you did not order. Plans changed without warning. Things you thought were settled came loose. On Saturday, December 5, 2026, the two points in the sky that the tradition holds responsible for that feeling both change sign at the same moment.

This guide explains what those two points are, what leaves your life that day, what arrives, and how long it lasts. Nothing here is a promise. It is what Vedic astrology reads from the sky by your Moon sign, and how to use it well.

sections.label: The two nodes
title: A head that wants,
a tail that lets go.
paragraphs: Rahu and Ketu are not planets you can see. They are the two points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path, which is why Western astrology calls them the north node and the south node of the Moon. Rahu is the north node and Ketu is the south node. They always sit exactly opposite each other, and they always change sign together.

The tradition pictures them as a dragon cut in two. Rahu is the head with no body: all appetite, always wanting more, never quite full. Wherever he sits, life is read as louder, hungrier and less predictable. Ketu is the tail with no head: he does not crave and does not chase. Wherever he sits, you are said to loosen your grip and care less.

They spend about a year and a half in each sign, so a change of sign is one of the bigger turns of the calendar. For each Moon sign it moves the appetite to one part of life and the letting go to the opposite part.

sections.label: What ends
title: The sudden shocks
ease off.
paragraphs: Since May 18, 2025, Rahu has been in your house of sudden change, the eighth house counted from your Moon sign. That house covers what you cannot plan for: upheavals, things that end without notice, other people's money, the fears you keep to yourself. With the hungry head in it, the tradition reads a stretch of jolts and of worrying about what might come next.
Over the same months Ketu sat in your house of money and family, the second house. That is read as feeling a little cut off from your own savings, your family table, or even your own voice.

On December 5 both leave. The tradition does not say life becomes quiet overnight, but the particular feeling of waiting for the next surprise is read as easing from that day. If the last year and a half taught you to stay calm when the floor moves, you keep that.

sections.label: What begins
title: Who you let in,
and who you become.
paragraphs: Rahu moves into your house of partnership, the seventh house from your Moon sign. The appetite lands on the people closest to you: a partner, a future partner, a business partner. This is read as a strong wish for a real, committed other half, and often as an interest in someone unlike your usual type: another background, another city, another way of living. For people already with someone, it is read as the relationship asking for more room and more honesty.

At the same moment Ketu arrives on Cancer itself, your own sign. This is the letting go landing on you. You may want more space than usual, care less about how you come across, and feel that an older version of you no longer fits. Its useful side is real: the tradition reads it as clearing out the roles you play only to please people, so that whoever comes close meets the person you really are.
Put together, the next chapter is about two questions. Who do you let in? And which old picture of yourself do you put down?

rows.note: Rahu entered your house of sudden change and Ketu your house of money and family.
A Saturday. Rahu enters your house of partnership and Ketu arrives on your own sign, at the same moment.
Read as a time for partnership to become a main subject of your life, and for a quieter, less performed version of you.
Both move on again, and this chapter closes.

steps.name: Let people in slowly
steps.text: The pull toward someone can be strong and fast in these months. Enjoy it, and give big promises time. A person who is right for you is still right three months later.

steps.name: Notice the pattern you are leaving
steps.text: Write down one way you used to act only to keep others comfortable. That is the old you this period is read as loosening. You do not have to replace it with anything yet.

steps.name: Keep room for yourself
steps.text: Wanting space is part of this chapter, not a problem with your relationship. Say it plainly, so the people close to you do not read silence as distance.

steps.name: Be careful with joint commitments
steps.text: Shared money, contracts and business partnerships deserve a second reading and a second opinion while the appetite sits in this house.

faq.q: Is this for my Sun sign or my Moon sign?
faq.a: Your Moon sign. Vedic astrology reads timing from the sign the Moon was in when you were born, which is often different from the Sun sign most people know.

faq.q: Are Rahu and Ketu the same as the north and south node?
faq.a: Yes. Rahu is the Moon's north node and Ketu is its south node. Vedic astrology uses the sidereal zodiac, so the sign they are in can differ from the one a Western chart shows.

faq.q: Does this mean I will meet someone after December 5?
faq.a: No one can promise that. The tradition reads these eighteen months as a time when partnership matters more to you and unusual people catch your interest. What you do with it, and your own birth chart, decide the rest.

note: Dates are US Eastern time. Vedic (sidereal) astrology, read by Moon sign.
